Southeast.text: Spot cotton trading was active. Supplies and producer offerings were moderate. Demand was good. Average local spot prices were higher. Trading of CCC-loan equities were inactive. Daytime temperatures across the lower Southeast cotton-producing regions ranged from the upper 40s to mid-70s, while nighttime lows generally fluctuated from the upper 30s to lower 50s. Limited precipitation was received across much of the region, with only scattered light showers reported in some areas late in the period. Mostly favorable weather conditions prevailed throughout the week, allowing harvesting, module transportation, and ginning activities to continue. Open weather conditions supported harvest progress throughout the region. Producers continued to benefit from generally dry field conditions as harvest advanced where fields remained accessible. Daytime temperatures across the upper Southeast cotton-producing regions ranged from the upper 40s to lower 70s, while overnight lows generally fluctuated from the upper 30s to lower 50s. Weather conditions varied across the region during the reporting period. Portions of eastern and central North Carolina received measurable rainfall, with around one and one-half inches reported near Raleigh, while areas of South Carolina remained comparatively drier, with approximately one-quarter of an inch of moisture reported near Florence, SC. Despite localized rainfall, harvesting, module transportation, and ginning activities continued where field conditions allowed. Producers in Virginia and much of the Carolinas benefited from seasonable temperatures and harvest advanced as fields dried following precipitation events. Overall, weather-related interruptions were limited, though progress varied depending on local rainfall amounts and field accessibility.

North Delta.text: Trading of spot cotton and CCC-loan equities was active. Supplies and producer offerings were light. Demand was good. Average local spot prices were higher. Business activity had begun to increase. Sunny skies interspersed with periods of cloudiness prevailed throughout most of the reporting period. Daytime high temperatures in the 70s dipped into the lower 40s and 50s, while nighttime lows in the low-to-mid 50s fell into the 30s. Rainfall entered the region on Sunday, November 22, and Wednesday, November 25, bringing cooler temperatures and brisk winds to portions of the territory. According to meteorologists, snow flurries were forecast for Thanksgiving Day, November 26 in portions of Arkansas and Missouri. A potential mix of rain and snow were expected to move through the Mid-South, accompanied by increasing wind gusts of 20 to 30 mph. Accumulated precipitation measured from trace amounts to more than one-quarter of an inch of rain. Forecast rainfall later in the week was expected to provide much-needed moisture to drought-affected fields. No outdoor activities were reported. Crop establishment and field preparations had been completed prior to freezing temperatures. The volume of cotton on gin yards continued to decline as ginning operations neared completion. Some gins operated on 24-hour shifts and others only on two shifts.

East Texas-South Texas.text: Spot cotton trading was active. Supplies and producer offerings were moderate. Demand was light. Average local spot prices were higher. Trading of CCC-loan equities was inactive. There was no new forward contracting activity reported, but producers delivered on previously established contracts. Foreign mill inquiries were light to moderate. Interest was best from India, Pakistan, and Vietnam. In East Texas, South Texas, and the Upper Coast, weather conditions were partly cloudy, with intermittent showers occurring throughout the reporting period. Daytime highs ranged from the upper 40s to the lower 80s, while nighttime lows fluctuated from the 30s to 60s. A cold front moved into the region early in the period, bringing scattered showers and light rainfall accumulations. The heaviest accumulations were reported near Corpus Christi, where amounts ranged from around three-quarters of an inch to one inch of moisture. Gins continued operating at a steady pace, though the season neared the end as seed cotton supplies diminished. Some gins completed seasonal operations. Most facilities suspended operations on Thursday, November 26, in observance of the Thanksgiving holiday. In the Rio Grande Valley, daytime highs were in the upper 50s to lower 80s, and overnight lows ranged from the 40s to 60s. Scattered showers were received. The winter moisture was welcomed, but more rainfall will be needed ahead of spring planting, scheduled to begin in February. The warehouses remained busy fulfilling shipping orders during the week of the Thanksgiving holiday.

Yields and quality varied considerably, with higher-than-normal leaf content attributed to regrowth following rainfall events. Defoliation challenges persisted, with some fields requiring three applications to promote leaf drop. Producers received a hard overnight freeze to aid defoliation on November 23, that tied unofficially for the latest first freeze of the season for Lubbock, according to local news outlets. Gins increased heat in dryer systems to manage excessive moisture in seed cotton, resulting in slower ginning rates. Most gins adjusted operating schedules based on module availability and the Thanksgiving holiday on November 26. In Kansas, drizzly, damp, and windy weather persisted, with daytime temperatures ranging from the low 40s to u p per 60s and nighttime lows fluctuating between the 2 0s and 50s. Despite these difficulties, harvest progress slowly advanced. All gins offered pressing services, although some had caught up with available module supplies on gin yards, allowing employees time to observe the Thanksgiving holiday. Desert Southwest (DSW).text: Spot cotton trading was inactive. Supplies and producer offerings were light. Demand was light. No forward contracting was reported during the period. Average local spot prices were higher. Foreign mill inquiries were light. In the DSW, predominantly sunny to partly cloudy skies prevailed throughout the reporting period. Daytime temperatures ranged from the 60s to the 70s, while nighttime lows were mostly in the 30s to 50s. No measurable precipitation was reported. Harvest activities continued in Arizona. According to local sources, recent rainfall negatively impacted yields in the Safford Valley, with reports of lint remaining on the ground following heavy rainfall. Module trucks continued hauling seed cotton to gin yards for processing. Ginning proceeded at a steady pace in central Arizona, El Paso, TX, and New Mexico. According to sources, producers in the El Paso area have been pleased with the quality of the crop.

San Joaquin Valley (SJV).text: Spot cotton trading was inactive. Supplies and demand were light. No forward contracting or domestic mill activity was reported. Average local spot prices were higher. Foreign mill inquiries were light. Mostly cloudy to partly cloudy skies prevailed across the San Joaquin Valley during the week, with scattered rainfall occurring intermittently throughout the reporting period, with more rain chances in the nearby forecast. Daytime temperatures ranged from the upper 50s to the mid-60s, while overnight lows were mostly in the 30s and 40s. Accumulated precipitation generally ranged from one-quarter of an inch to approximately three-quarters of an inch. Harvest neared completion in Tulare and Kern Counties, with only a limited number of acres remaining unharvested. Modules continued to accumulate on gin yards awaiting processing. Early in the reporting period, wet road conditions slowed the movement of modules to gins; however, transportation improved as conditions dried. Gins operated around the clock on multiple shifts to process seed cotton as efficiently as possible.

American Pima (AP).text: Spot cotton trading was inactive. Supplies were moderate. Demand was light. No forward contracting or domestic mill activity was reported. Average local spot prices were steady. Mill inquiries were moderate. Daytime highs in the Far West ranged from the 50s to the 70s, while nighttime lows were mostly in the 30s to 50s. Harvesting continued in the Safford Valley. Reports indicated some potential yield loss following heavy rainfall, which left lint on the ground in affected fields. Early in the reporting period, wet field conditions temporarily slowed the movement of module trucks as seed cotton was collected from fields. As conditions dried and soils firmed, collection resumed at a steady pace. Gins continued processing modules stored on gin yards throughout the Desert Southwest region. In the San Joaquin Valley, harvest was virtually complete, with only a limited number of acres remaining unharvested. Gins operated at full capacity, processing modules stored on gin yards. Wet field conditions at the beginning of the reporting period briefly hindered module retrieval from harvested fields; however, warm, dry weather improved field access, allowing pickup activities to return to a normal pace.
